title: Identifying State Dependence in Brand Choice: Evidence from Hurricanes
eligible_reason: Main estimator is generalized synthetic control (gsynth, force='time', CV over r in {0,1}) on household x hurricane units indexed by week relative to the storm (running_wk). Comparison TWFE columns in Table 3 (felm treated_period | period + id) and the Figure A2 event study (felm wk_ref + treated_wk_ref | id) are also in event time: each treated household-hurricane unit is treated at relative week 0, with hurricane-specific control households. This is a stacked event-time design with a single cohort in the estimating time index and no calendar-time FE. Nielsen data are not shipped.
design_notes: build/ constructs household-hurricane-week panels from Nielsen HomeScan and RMS plus public HURDAT2. analysis/run_all.R: run_gsynth for 10 outcomes (trip_upc_skip, trip_brand_skip, persistence, quantities, prices); synth_res.R makes Table 3 by combining gsynth ATTs with run_reg specs 'means', 'did', 'twoway' (treated_period | period + id) and 'twoway_plus' (adds treated-specific quadratic trends). sd_comparison.R (Table 4) compares to structural estimates (mcmc_estimation.R).
n_eligible_specs_note: Stacked event-time design; gsynth main estimator.
n_adoption_cohorts_note: In event time all treated household-hurricane units are treated at running_wk 0. Hurricanes span multiple calendar dates, but each has its own stacked control set.
modern_estimator_note: gsynth (Xu 2017) is not an admitted modern DiD estimator under the protocol.

specs.notes: Excluded: stacked event-time design without calendar-time FE; Nielsen data not shipped.

data_access: licensed (Nielsen HomeScan and RMS via Kilts Center); public HURDAT2
data_files_note: No data files in the package. Nielsen-derived .RData files are referenced but not included.
screener_notes: Screened from package only (no article text).
